newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq condemns visit by U.S. officials to n. Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Iraq condemns visit by U.S. officials to n. Iraq.

text.p: Iraq has condemned a visit by two senior U.S. officials to northern Iraq, saying their presence there was illegal and a violation of Iraqi sovereignty.
Baghdad newspaper on Friday, carrying a statement by a foreign ministry spokesman, said:

"The government of the Republic of Iraq again reaffirms its denunciation and disapporval of such irresponsible American practices carried out within the series of aggressive actions of interference in Iraq's domestic affairs."
The papers said U.S. presence in the area was "a cover to continue conspiracies against the steadfast Iraq, threaten its sovereignty and territorial integrity".
On Thursday the State Department said two senior U.S. officials were in northern Iraq talking to leaders of the two rival Kurdish factions there.

David Welch, acting assistant secretary of state for Near Eastern affairs, and Robert Deutsch, head of the State Department's Iran and Iraq office, were meeting leaders of the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) and Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK), a spokesman said.
The papers said the officials' entry into northern Iraq was illegal. Foreigners entering Iraq without a visa face prison terms of up to eight years if caught and convicted.

The KDP and PUK battled for two months last year in northern Iraq, which has effectively been under Western protection since 1991, after the KDP sought aid from Iraqi forces to help it capture the city of Arbil from its rival.
The United States brokered a ceasefire in October, and the two groups have been conducting sporadic peace talks in Ankara since.
Iraqi papers said the U.S. was sending its envoys to the area in order to prevent the Kurds from coming to terms with the central government in Baghdad.

State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said Thursday's talks, which also involved representatives of the Turkoman and Assyrian minorities in the area, were "focusing on the Ankara peace process" but gave no further details.
The KDP walked out of the Ankara talks last month, accusing the PUK of killing one of its officials in the Iraqi Kurdish town of Halabja. The PUK denied the charge.
